chunks: From him, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليهما السلام, that ʿAlī عليه السلام said:

“The milk of a baby girl and her urine are such that the garment is washed from them before she begins to eat, because her milk comes forth from her mother’s bladder. But the milk of a baby boy—before he begins to eat—the garment is not washed from it, nor from his urine, because the milk of the baby boy comes forth from the upper arms and the shoulders.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What this report contains—namely, that the garment is not washed from the urine of the infant boy before he begins to eat—means that it is sufficient for water to be poured over it, even if it is not wrung out, as al-Ḥalabī clarified in his earlier narration.

key_terms.الثَّوْبُ: the garment or cloth requiring purification
key_terms.بَوْلُهَا: her urine; referring to the baby girl’s urine
key_terms.لَبَنُ: milk; here, the milk of an infant as discussed in the ruling
key_terms.يُصَبَّ: to be poured; here, water being poured over the impurity
key_terms.يُغْسَلُ: it is washed; indicating the act of ritual cleaning

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about washing a garment stained by the urine of an infant before he or she begins to eat?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a fiqh ruling concerning purification of garments affected by the urine or milk of infant children before they begin eating food. The closing statement clarifies that in the case of the infant boy, the intended meaning is that pouring water over the garment is sufficient without wringing it out.
